title: Scaling curve compiler and SLA translator for tenant throughput profiles
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Design and implement a compiler that translates high-level tenant throughput SLAs and declarative autoscale profiles into runtime-ready scaling curves and safety envelopes. The output will be a compact policy artifact consumed by the autoscaling controller to make per-tenant scaling decisions: target_metric selectors, multi-phase scaling curves (linear / sigmoid / capped exponential), burst window definitions, and hard safety fences (min/max replicas, surge caps, cooldowns). This work bridges product-facing SLA primitives with the fleet controller semantics used by Dedicated capacity.
tasks: Define declarative schema for tenant throughput SLAs and profile primitives (targets, burst, penalty, fairness)
Prototype curve compiler that emits time-series-friendly scaling points and safety parameters
Integrate compiler output with the autoscaler policy runtime (policy loader + versioning)
Add validation and static checks: detect incompatible SLAs, unbounded surge, and missing safety fences
Add e2e tests with synthetic tenant workloads and Canary harness in staging
Instrument metrics and dashboards to surface compiler decisions, chosen curve, and safety triggers
Document API surface and provide example policies for common workloads (latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, bursty-PLG)
acceptance_criteria: Compiler accepts declarative SLA JSON/YAML and outputs a signed policy artifact with unique version ID
Autoscaler consumes policy artifact and enforces scaling curves and safety fences in staging for 5 synthetic tenants
No uncontrolled surge: scaling events must respect configured surge caps in 100% of staged tests
Dashboard shows per-tenant selected target metric, curve type, predicted capacity, and last enforced safety fence
Rollback path: a previous policy version can be re-applied without cluster instability
Performance: Compiler end-to-end latency < 200ms for typical SLA payloads and < 2s for complex profiles
comments: 2025-11-12 Aditi Rao: Initial ticket created after PM review. Goal is to provide deterministic translation from product SLA to runtime policy.
2025-11-18 Marco Gutierrez: Draft schema v0.1 attached in Confluence; pushing to prototype compiler. Noted potential ambiguity for 'burst window' semantics across heterogeneous GPU fleets.
2025-11-24 Design feedback (Lina Park): Recommend 'graceful decay' parameter to avoid oscillations when tenants drop traffic quickly. Added to schema v0.2.
2025-11-30 Infra review (Omar Singh): Need to ensure policy artifact size is bounded for controller cache. Added compression + version TTL requirement.

2025-12-03 QA: First staging run completed. Two issues found: 1) sigmoid curve parameters interpreted differently by controller when sequence_length variance is high; 2) missing explicit min_replicas caused tiny tenants to be scaled to zero causing cold-start regressions. Both flagged as tasks.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: expose many knobs for flexibility vs. provide opinionated presets. We'll ship with three preset profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and allow advanced custom policies behind an enterprise flag.
Decision: curve compiler will export both a human-readable policy JSON and a compact binary encoding for the controller. Binary encoding will include a checksum and semantic version.
Operational constraint: policy loader must support atomic swaps and graceful deprecation to avoid thrashing during large rollout.
Security: artifacts are written to S3 with customer-specific KMS encryption (private deployments) and signed by platform key for hosted deployments. Key rotation and verification need test coverage.
review_feedback: PM (Ruth Ellis): Ensure UI can surface why a tenant hit safety fence and recommended remediation.
SRE (Kai Matsuda): Add circuit-breaker that pauses scaling for a tenant if repeated oscillation events detected within 5 minutes.
Security (Nina Fong): Confirm that policy artifacts do not leak tenant identifiers when logged; use anonymized IDs in telemetry.
